title: MSTP (Multiple Spanning Tree)
description: Understand MSTP regions and configure Multiple Spanning Tree instances.
scenario: Understand MSTP regions and configure Multiple Spanning Tree instances.

concepts.title: What is MSTP?
concepts.body: MSTP (802.1s) is a spanning tree that can create multiple "instances". Each instance runs its own STP, grouping several VLANs together for better realistic control.
concepts.code:
Instance 0 → default (all VLANs)
Instance 1 → VLAN 10-20
Instance 2 → VLAN 30-40

concepts.title: MST Regions
concepts.body: Switches belong to a region if they share the same name, revision number, and instance-to-VLAN mapping. MSTP only sends BPDUs once per region.
concepts.code:
SW1(config)# spanning-tree mode mst
SW1(config)# spanning-tree mst configuration
SW1(config-mst)# name CCNA
SW1(config-mst)# revision 1

concepts.title: Instance Mapping
concepts.body: Map VLANs to instances inside MST config. Instance 0 is the default and handles all unmapped VLANs.
concepts.code:
SW1(config-mst)# instance 1 vlan 10-20
SW1(config-mst)# instance 2 vlan 30-40

concepts.title: Root per Instance
concepts.body: Each instance elects its own root bridge on every switch in the region.
